external_entities.name: reader
external_entities.description: A person who accesses the public site and may be signed in.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Public site: readers hit the web server over HTTPS, some of them signed in.

external_entities.name: admin
external_entities.description: An administrator who maintains the database directly.
external_entities.source_excerpt: There is an admin who maintains the database directly rather than through the CMS.

external_entities.name: CDN
external_entities.description: The CDN from which readers fetch images, stylesheets and downloads, and which has a bucket receiving newly published assets.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.

processes.name: web server
processes.description: The web server runs the CMS, serves the public site, and pushes newly published assets to the CDN.
processes.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS and keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database on the same hosted network.

data_stores.name: MySQL database
data_stores.description: A MySQL database holding pages, accounts and comments.
data_stores.source_excerpt: keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database on the same hosted network.
data_stores.notes: The source says: "I could not tell you whether the database is encrypted on disk."

data_stores.name: CDN bucket
data_stores.description: The CDN bucket receiving newly published images, stylesheets and downloads.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web server pushes them up to the CDN's bucket.

data_flows.name: visit site
data_flows.description: Readers access the public site through the web server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: readers hit the web server over HTTPS

data_flows.name: fetch assets
data_flows.description: Readers fetch images, stylesheets and downloads from the CDN.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.

data_flows.name: keep content
data_flows.description: The web server keeps pages, accounts and comments in the MySQL database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS and keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database

data_flows.name: publish assets
data_flows.description: The web server pushes newly published assets to the CDN bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When new assets are published the web server pushes them up to the CDN's bucket.
data_flows.notes: The source says: "Nothing here tells you how the push to the CDN is authenticated."
data_flows.data_description: newly published images, stylesheets and downloads

data_flows.name: maintain database
data_flows.description: The admin directly maintains the MySQL database from wherever they happen to be.
data_flows.source_excerpt: That is an unsecured MySQL connection straight to the box, no TLS on it
data_flows.notes: There is no jump host. The source says the admin connects from "wherever they happen to be".

trust_boundaries.name: hosted network
trust_boundaries.description: The hosted network containing the web server and MySQL database.

trust_boundaries.name: CDN
trust_boundaries.description: The trust zone associated with the externally operated CDN and its bucket.

assumptions.assumption: The web server is reachable from the internet because it serves the public site that readers access.
assumptions.basis: The source describes a "Public site" whose readers hit the web server over HTTPS.

assumptions.assumption: The CDN is controlled by a different party from the hosted network, so it forms a tenant trust boundary.
assumptions.basis: The source names a separate CDN and refers to its bucket as "the CDN's bucket".

assumptions.assumption: The CDN bucket is in the CDN trust zone because it is explicitly identified as the CDN's bucket.
assumptions.basis: The source says the web server pushes assets to "the CDN's bucket."

assumptions.assumption: The CDN presents published assets as public because readers fetch the images, stylesheets and downloads from it.
assumptions.basis: The source says readers fetch the bucket's images, stylesheets and downloads.
